title: Published Oklahoma tapered ETAS fits give 5.5-6.0 years for 95 percent of M5-root sequences to end when new background events stop
abstract: We calculated the time of the last descendant after one M5 initiating earthquake under three published Oklahoma tapered ETAS fits. New background events were set to zero. Space was unbounded and fitted productivity stayed constant. A probability integral equation included all generations and the published future-magnitude law. The direct taper was 371-405 days, but 95 percent of sequences ended within 5.5-6.0 years. The chance of a nominal M2.5+ event after five years was 7.0-9.2 percent, against 0.19-0.29 percent for direct offspring only. For the fit through 2020, the chance of an M5+ descendant after five years was 0.00069. Independent simulations of 100,000 sequences and a mesh refinement agreed with the solver. A 15 percent increase of productivity raised the 95 percent completion time from 5.5 to 10.4 years. We provide code, licensed aggregate input parameters, numerical checks and scenario results. The result is a consequence of the fitted model, not new evidence about an observed shutdown. The calculation does not include continuing external forcing, parameter uncertainty, finite spatial boundaries or the longer large-parent kernels. A direct taper does not specify a whole-sequence completion time or a safe well-closure interval.

display.caption: Probability of a late descendant and 95 percent sequence-completion times for an M5 root. New background events are zero. Space is unbounded. Fitted temporal and productivity parameters remain constant.
